metaDescription: We evaluated six rain barrels, rigid and collapsible, on capacity, screens, overflow, lids and stands to help you collect roof water for your garden.
expertTake: The RTS Home Accents Newport 50 gallon barrel is our best overall pick because it combines a removable lid, a screen kit, a stand and a flexible overflow nozzle. The RTS flat back walnut model is the value pick for tight spots against a wall. Anyone who has no downspout access or lives where roof water collection is restricted should skip the barrel and check local rules first.
introParagraphs: A rain barrel catches runoff from a downspout and stores it for the garden. It is a simple way to soften your water use, give plants unchlorinated water, and keep a reserve for dry spells without running the tap.

Barrels differ in more than size. The lid, the screen that keeps out debris and mosquitoes, the overflow outlet and the height of the spigot decide how well a barrel works day to day. A stand raises the spigot so a hose or can can actually fill.

products.name: RTS Home Accents Newport 50 Gallon Rain Barrel with Stand
products.description:
The Newport is a 50 gallon rigid barrel in a bronze finish, supplied with a stand. A removable lid gives you access for cleaning, and a screen kit on top keeps leaves and debris out of the stored water. The overflow nozzle can be installed on either side, so you can aim excess water away from the house or link a second barrel.

The tradeoff is that at 50 gallons it fills quickly in a storm, and a single barrel does not store much compared with a large cistern. Against the Step2 Fernway, which is also 50 gallons but has a stainless steel screen and sells the stand separately, the Newport bundles the stand and is easier to set up as a ready kit. It is a good fit for one downspout and a small to mid-sized garden.

Ownership means regular cleaning. Check the screen for debris, clean the interior once a season, make sure the spigot does not drip, and in freezing climates empty and disconnect the barrel for winter so the plastic does not crack.
products.bestFor: One-downspout gardens that want a complete, ready-to-set-up barrel.
pros: Removable lid makes cleaning the interior straightforward
Included screen kit keeps leaves and debris out
Overflow nozzle can be fitted on either side for flexible routing
Stand is included, so the spigot sits high enough to use
cons: Fifty gallons fills fast and stores modest volume
Needs draining before freezing weather to avoid cracks

products.name: RTS Home Accents 50 Gallon Flat Back Rain Barrel, Walnut
products.description:
This RTS barrel is a flat back design in a walnut colour, with a 50 gallon capacity, UV-resistant polyethylene and a built-in overflow valve. The flat back sits flush against a wall or beside a downspout, saving the space a round barrel would take. A stand is included, and you can link multiple barrels through the overflow.

The tradeoff is the lid and cleaning access. Compared with the Newport, which has a removable lid, a flat back barrel can be harder to scrub inside, and its shape limits how much you can reach. It also stores the same 50 gallons, so a flat back is about layout, not volume. It suits tight side yards and patios.

Flush the barrel regularly, keep the screen clear, and check the overflow hose. Empty it before winter so freezing water does not stress the seams.
products.bestFor: Tight side yards and patios where a flush, wall-hugging shape matters.
pros: Flat back sits flush against walls and downspouts
UV-resistant polyethylene resists sun fading and cracking
Built-in overflow valve manages excess water safely
Stand included for easy filling of watering cans
cons: Interior can be harder to scrub than a wide-open barrel
Same 50 gallon volume as round designs, so shape is the only gain

products.name: RTS Home Accents ECO 50 Gallon Rain Barrel, Recycled Plastic
products.description:
The ECO is a flat back 50 gallon barrel made entirely from recycled plastic, with a UV-resistant polyethylene body and a built-in overflow valve that lets you connect multiple barrels. It is aimed at gardeners who care about material sourcing and want the same compact shape as the other RTS flat back barrel.

The tradeoff is that recycled plastic does not change how the barrel works, and the listing offers few extras. Compared with the Newport, it lacks the removable lid and screen kit highlighted there, so debris control depends on the included screen and your own care. It is a sound, simple barrel for a modest garden.

Check the screen regularly, scrub the interior each season, and empty the barrel before hard freezes. Keep it out of deep shade where algae can grow if sunlight reaches the water.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who prefer recycled materials in a compact flat back shape.
pros: Made from recycled plastic for a lower material footprint
Flat back saves space beside a wall or downspout
Overflow valve lets you chain multiple barrels
UV-resistant body handles full sun without fading fast
cons: Fewer features than the Newport, with no removable lid highlighted
Fifty gallons fills quickly in a heavy storm

products.name: Step2 Fernway 50 Gallon Plastic Rain Barrel
products.description:
The Step2 Fernway holds 50 gallons and uses a stainless steel mesh screen that the listing says allows maximum water flow while filtering fine particulate. A compatible stand is sold separately and raises the barrel to improve pressure, and you can link multiple barrels for more storage.

The tradeoff is that the stand costs extra, and without it the spigot sits low. Compared with the RTS Newport, which bundles a stand, the Fernway is cheaper to start but needs a block, stand or platform to be useful. The stainless screen is a real plus for debris and mosquito control, and Step2 is a known plastics maker.

Clean the screen regularly, flush the interior each season, and keep the spigot free of grit. Drain it before freezing, and elevate it on a level, solid base.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who value a stainless screen and already have a base or stand.
pros: Stainless steel screen filters fine debris well
Compatible stand raises the spigot for better water pressure

Fifty gallon capacity suits a single downspout
cons: Stand costs extra, so the spigot sits low without it

products.name: SQUEEZE master 50 Gallon Rain Barrel with Diverter
products.description:
The SQUEEZE master is a 50 gallon barrel in UV-resistant, anti-freeze polypropylene, with a water diverter included and a mesh top to keep out debris and mosquitoes. The diverter connects the downspout to the barrel, which makes installation more straightforward if you do not want to cut your downspout yourself.

The tradeoff is that the stand is not included, so you will need to raise it yourself. Compared with the RTS Newport, the SQUEEZE master bundles a diverter rather than a stand, so the work differs. The anti-freeze rating is a plus in cold climates, but you should still drain it before a hard freeze.

Clean the mesh each month, check the diverter for leaks, scrub the interior once a season and keep the barrel level.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a diverter included and need to build their own stand.
pros: Included diverter simplifies connecting to the downspout
Anti-freeze polypropylene is more forgiving in cold weather
Mesh top blocks debris and mosquitoes
UV-resistant body suits full-sun placement
cons: No stand included, so you must raise the barrel yourself
Fifty gallons fills quickly during heavy rain

products.name: Laspeiraux Collapsible 53 Gallon Rain Barrel
products.description:
The Laspeiraux is a collapsible 53 gallon barrel made from three-layer PVC, with an integrated screw-in faucet. It folds flat for storage and carrying, which suits renters, small spaces and seasonal use. The listing positions it as a portable alternative to bulky rigid barrels.

The tradeoff is durability and set-up. Flexible PVC bulges when full and can be punctured or degrade in sun, and without a rigid stand the faucet sits low. Compared with the RTS Newport, it is easier to store but less robust, and it is not meant to sit through a freeze. It suits temporary or movable setups.

Empty and dry it before folding to avoid mildew. Keep it out of prolonged direct sun if the manufacturer advises, check seams and the faucet connection, and store it away from sharp objects.
products.bestFor: Renters and anyone who needs a barrel that folds away between seasons.
pros: Folds flat for easy storage and carrying
Fifty-three gallon capacity matches rigid barrels
Integrated screw-in faucet simplifies setup
Light enough to move without help
cons: Flexible PVC is less durable than rigid polyethylene
Faucet sits low without a raised platform

buyingCriteria.explanation: A roof collects far more water than a single barrel holds: a modest roof sheds hundreds of gallons in a moderate storm. A 50 gallon barrel like the Newport fills quickly, so plan an overflow route or link a second barrel. Buy size to match your garden's real use, not the roof's yield.

An open barrel breeds mosquitoes within days. A fine screen, like the Step2 stainless mesh or the Newport screen kit, keeps out larvae and leaves. A removable lid, as on the Newport, makes cleaning much easier. Skip any barrel without a fully screened inlet.

When a barrel fills, the overflow decides where the extra water goes. A nozzle that can be fitted on either side, as on the Newport, gives flexibility. Linkable overflows, as on the RTS and Step2 models, let you chain barrels. Point overflow away from your foundation.

Rain barrels work by gravity, so a higher spigot gives more pressure and room to fill a can. The Newport and RTS flat back include a stand, while the Fernway and SQUEEZE master do not. A stand holds a full barrel that weighs hundreds of pounds, so it must be level and solid.

UV-resistant polyethylene or polypropylene resists sun damage and cracking for years. Flexible PVC, as on the Laspeiraux, folds away but ages faster. Dark opaque barrels also limit algae growth by keeping sunlight out of the water.

Collection is legal in most places but some jurisdictions limit it, so check local rules. Rainwater from roofs is for gardens, not drinking. Avoid using it on edible leaves unless you understand the risks from roofing materials and bird droppings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Debris and mosquito control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared screens, lids and inlets from published specifications. The Step2 stainless mesh and the Newport screen kit scored well. Open or loosely screened designs were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Setup and installation
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked what comes in the box, such as stands and diverters. The Newport and RTS flat back include stands, while the SQUEEZE master includes a diverter. Missing pieces were counted as extra work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Overflow and linking
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at overflow placement and whether barrels can be chained. The Newport's two-sided nozzle and the linkable RTS and Step2 designs rated best. A poor overflow was treated as a flooding risk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and weather resistance
howWeEvaluated.description: We researched UV resistance, freeze behaviour and expected life. Rigid polyethylene and polypropylene scored well, while flexible PVC was noted for sun and puncture risk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We asked how easy each barrel is to clean inside, using owner feedback patterns. A removable lid, as on the Newport, makes this simple. Flat back and sealed designs were noted for harder access.

maintenance.why: Leaves and grit clog the mesh and reduce flow. A clear screen also stops mosquitoes.
Sediment builds up and can clog the spigot. A scrub keeps water cleaner.
Drips waste water and hint at failing washers. Replace worn parts promptly.
Ice expands and cracks plastic. Disconnect the diverter and leave the tap open.
A full barrel weighs hundreds of pounds. A shifting base can tip it.

faq.q: Is a rain barrel worth it?
faq.a: For a garden, yes, because it gives you free, soft water and a reserve for dry spells. It will not replace mains water for a large lawn. Most kits use either a diverter that replaces a section of the downspout or a flexible hose that feeds the barrel's inlet. Cut the downspout a little above the barrel top, fit the diverter, and make sure the overflow hose points away from the foundation. If you are unsure about cutting metal, ask a handyman, since a poorly aimed overflow can soak the base of the wall.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a rain barrel?
faq.a: A collapsible barrel costs the least, while a rigid barrel with a stand costs more. Spend for the lid, screen and stand rather than for style. That depends on how much you water. A single 50 gallon barrel suits a few containers and raised beds, but it empties in a couple of watering sessions. Linking two or three barrels through their overflows gives you a more useful reserve, and a larger roof area makes extra storage worthwhile because a single storm can fill several barrels in an hour.

faq.q: How long does a rain barrel last?
faq.a: A rigid UV-resistant barrel can last many years if drained before freezing. Flexible PVC lasts fewer seasons. Yes, raising it on a level, solid base gives the tap enough height to fill a can and gives gravity some pressure for a soaker hose. A full 50 gallon barrel holds roughly four hundred pounds of water, so use concrete blocks, a purpose-built stand or a firm paved pad, and check that it cannot tip when it fills.

faq.q: Does a rain barrel attract mosquitoes?
faq.a: Only if it is open. A fine screen over the inlet and a closed lid prevent mosquitoes from laying eggs.

faq.q: Is rainwater safe to use on vegetables?
faq.a: Use it at the soil level and avoid wetting edible leaves, since roof runoff can carry contaminants. Never drink it. Check local guidance if you are unsure.

faq.q: Is rain collection legal where I live?
faq.a: In most places yes, but some areas limit how much you can store or how you use it. Check your local rules before installing a barrel.
